args.root_cause: A config change to server.properties applied at the ~07:33:08 restart set white-list=true and enforce-whitelist=true while whitelist.json was empty ([]). Every player (Alex_Builds, Steve_Mines, newplayer01, newplayer02, ...) was rejected with "You are not whitelisted on this server!". The same change also raised max-players from 20 to 40, which looks intended and was kept.
args.actions: 1) Took baselines of status, logs and server.properties. 2) Saw players drop to 0. Logs showed a restart followed by "not whitelisted" rejections, and the diff of server.properties showed white-list=true, enforce-whitelist=true and max-players=40. whitelist.json was empty. 3) Declared the incident. 4) Ran console "whitelist off", which turned the whitelist off live with no restart and saved white-list=false to server.properties. 5) Edited server.properties to set enforce-whitelist back to its pre-incident value (false) and kept max-players=40. 6) Checked the result: Alex_Builds and Steve_Mines reconnected, new players join normally, TPS is 20, and all plugins are enabled.
args.residual_risk: I don't know who or what made the config change. If it was meant to start a whitelist, whitelist.json has to be filled with players before it is turned on again. The running server still holds enforce-whitelist=true in memory until the next restart; this does nothing while the whitelist is off. The max-players=40 change was kept on the assumption that it was intended.
